title: Response Token Autopsy — Wires, interaction notes, and grooming
content:
Purpose:
Quick working doc for the 'token autopsy' flow — an interactive viewer to inspect a single invocation at token granularity, surface cost and latency contributions, and provide actionable remediation suggestions. Aim is to create a low-friction UX for engineers and SREs to diagnose expensive invocations and drive optimizations back into routing, prompts, batching, or quantization profiles.

Audience:
- Product/Console PMs and Designers
- Eng owners for telemetry, RPC, and runtime hooks (serving/runtime teams)
- Solutions & CS for customer debugging flows

Context / problem space (short):
Many customers ask: "Why did this single request cost X and take Y ms?" Current console rolls up costs per-invocation and per-model but lacks a live, explorable timeline for token-level behavior (e.g., tokenization spikes, sampling-induced latency, KV-cache misses, fallback model switches). We need a lightweight inspector that maps tokens -> cost/latency slices and suggests fixes.

Goals for MVP:
- Show token list with per-token latency and cost estimates (estimated GPU-micros + token-wise compute class).
- Link tokens to sampling events (logprobs, temperature spikes) and to runtime events (loader stalls, cache misses, kernel switch).
- Inline suggestions: batching tweak, prompt trim, quantization variant recommendation.
- Allow saving an invocation snapshot and sharing a short link with support.

Non-goals for MVP:
- Full token-level replay of model internals (no need for raw KV cache dumps yet).
- Synchronous live sampling for streaming invocations (we can do async saved snapshots first).

Wireframe iterations (A/B/C) — high level notes:
A) Compact table + inline sparkbars (fast scan)
- Left column: invocation header (invocation id, model, region, start/end timestamps, overall cost/latency).
- Middle: token list (compact rows). Each row: index, token text, token byte-size, token-cost (¢), token-latency (ms), small sparkbar for accumulation.
- Right: event panel (expandable): maps kernel switches, cache misses, queued time. Hover on event highlights affected token rows.
- Pros: very scannable, fits many tokens, fast discovery.
- Cons: harder to show long contextual annotations and sampling metadata.

B) Split-pane timeline + token-band (rich annotations)
- Top: timeline view (stacked bars: queuing, compute, data-load, sampling). Each bar is pannable; zoom controls (token granularity up to entire invocation).
- Bottom: token-band horizontally scrollable; tokens rendered as chips, color-coded by compute intensity. Clicking a chip opens a side drawer with metadata (logprob, top-k, post-processing hooks).
- Pros: intuitive temporal mapping and good for storytelling in Socratic debugging.
- Cons: space-hungry, more complex to implement.

C) Conversation-mode inspector (context-first)
- Shows the full conversation on left; tokens overlaid inline with micro-badges showing cost/latency. On selecting a micro-badge, a floating popover shows the per-token breakdown and recommended actions.
- Pros: aligns to how customers think (utterance-centric).
- Cons: token-level scanning is slower for long outputs.

Design decisions to resolve in grooming:
- Row density vs legibility: default to denser rows with an accessibility toggle to increase type and row height. (A11y requirement).
- Units for cost: show both estimated cents per token and normalized 'cost weight' (0-100) for fast triage.
- Derivation note: token cost = model-flop-estimate * runtime-cost-per-flop + amortized infra per-request overhead. Need to sync with telemetry owners (INF-2739) to finalize formula and confidence bands.
- Privacy: redact user PII tokens by default; provide masked/unmasked toggle in secure accounts only.

Interaction patterns / microcopy suggestions:
- Row hover hint: "Show token provenance & latency events"
- Empty state when sampling info missing: "Sampling traces unavailable for this invocation. Enable full trace collection in Dedicated or Private." (link to docs)
- Recommendation CTA: "Add to optimization playbook" — persists a short checklist (prompt trim suggested, enable KV caching, use model-v2-q4) that can be attached to a rollout.

Telemetry & backend hooks (engineering notes):
- Required traces: per-token timestamp (token_emitted_ts), token_enqueue_ts, kernel_start_ts, kernel_end_ts, kernel_type (quantized/float), sampled_top_k if available.
- Suggested backend summary: precompute token-rows and a condensed event map to avoid streaming thousands of rows to client. Provide paginated token pages for very long outputs.
- Perf SLO: inspector must open <200ms for invocations <=512 tokens (server-side prepared payload).
- API contract: /invocations/{id}/token-autopsy -> returns tokens[], events[], recommendations[] (we'll iterate on shape with infra). See GitHub PR: github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/487 for initial proto.

Backlog grooming (prioritized):
1) Basic compact table + precomputed token cost/latency — 3 points — blocker: telemetry schema (JIRA INF-2739).
2) Event mapping overlay + hover bindings — 5 points — needed for usefulness.
3) Share/save snapshot link + permission gating — 2 points.
4) Recommend engine (ruleset: prompt length heuristic, batch tuning, quantization fallback) — 3 points — requires integrate with Optimize.
5) Conversation-mode view + inline badges — 5 points (stretch).
6) Accessibility tuning and a11y QA — 2 points (must before GA).

Open questions / unresolved:
- How accurate do we need the per-token cost estimate to be for billing vs diagnosis? (billing-team input required)
- Can we rely on approximate kernel timing reported from the runtime, or do we need an aggregator to correct skew across GPUs? (ping infra/serving/runtime)
- Do we show tokenization implementation details (e.g., BPE split) or abstract tokens to text spans for non-technical users? (product decision)

Example vignette (user flow):
- Customer sees a spike in average invocation cost for model A. They open an invocation, click "Token autopsy". Compact table loads, they filter to tokens with latency > 10ms. Hovering token 134 highlights an upstream event: "KV cache miss (region eu-west-1)" and suggests: "Enable regional hot-cache or pin model in eu-west-1". They save snapshot and attach to a support ticket.

Notes from initial sync (2025-01-15) with runtime owners:
- Kernel_type tagging will be available in runtime v2.3 (target feb release). Need a feature flag until rollout.
- For now, runtime can emit coarse event buckets; detailed per-token timings in Dedicated only.

Next actions (owner: Aisha):
- Align with INF telemetry owner (Ethan) to finalize token cost formula (due 2025-01-17).
- Create PR for API proto + mock server response for designers to iterate (see PR #487).
- Schedule 30-min design handoff with serving-runtime and infra (Weds 2025-01-22).

Todos in doc (short):
- [ ] Finalize accessibility sizes and token density (design)
- [ ] Confirm telemetry keys and any sampling flags (engineering)
- [ ] Draft microcopy for recommendation CTA and empty states (content)
- [ ] Wire up share snapshot UX and short link semantics (product/eng)

Slack threads / references:
- #console-token-inspector (discussion thread: 2025-01-08 — notes attached)
- #runtime-traces (runtime owner sync: 2025-01-10)

Rough mock labels / UI copy suggestions (for designers/devs):
- "Token" column header tooltip: "The smallest unit the model saw (tokenization depends on model)."
- Token cost column header: "Estimated compute-related cost for this token. Does not include storage or network overhead."
- Event badges: small pill: e.g., "KV miss", "Kernel switch", "Queue" — with hover details and timestamp.

End notes:
This is an iterative, engineer-heavy feature that will be most useful when combined with saving & sharing snapshots (saves time for support). Prioritize the compact table MVP first so we can start collecting qualitative feedback from early customers.

Links referenced in-text:
- JIRA INF-2739 (telemetry schema)
- CONFLUENCE-Console/Token-Observability (design brief)
- github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/487 (proto + mock)
